recited poetry that preserved historical memory, expressed moral ideas, addressed political issues, and sometimes advised
rulers. Their works were transmitted orally and became part of the literary heritage of the Kazakh steppe. Unlike a modern
entertainer, a zhyrau could hold social and intellectual influence through the authority of words. The term is best retained in
English because “poet,” “bard,” or “singer” alone cannot fully express the combination of artistic, advisory, and public roles.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Akhmetzhanova, Z. K. (2012). Очерки по национальной концептологии. Repository record
     ●​   Zhumadil, A. “The Continuity of Kazakh Rituals and Traditions with Ancient Tribes of Kazakhstan.” Article record
     ●​   Supports: General context of Kazakh cultural concepts and historical traditions; these sources are not sufficient on
          their own to establish the full literary role of zhyraus.
     ●​   Verification status: Draft. A specialised literary-history source on zhyrau poetry, major historical zhyraus, and oral
          transmission is essential.

heading: Aqsúiek

category.title: Historical, Social and National Concepts
category.description: Institutions, identities and ideas from Kazakh history and society.

short: Aqsúiek literally means “white bone.” Historically, it referred to the aristocratic social category in Kazakh society, particularly lineages associated with Chinggisid descent and certain religiously prestigious groups.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Ақсүйек
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Aqsúiek
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /ɑqˈsʊjek/
     ●​   Word class: Noun; historical social-category term.
     ●​   Related forms: Ақ (aq, white); сүйек (súiek, bone); ақсүйектік (aqsúiektik, aristocratic status or aristocracy);
          қарасүйек (qarasúiek, commoner social category in historical usage).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Aqsúiek literally means “white bone.” Historically, it referred to the aristocratic social category in Kazakh society, particularly
lineages associated with Chinggisid descent and certain religiously prestigious groups. Its exact scope depends on the
historical context.
sections.Cultural context:
In traditional Kazakh social organisation, aqsúiek was used in contrast with qarasúiek. The category commonly included the
töre—descendants of Chinggis Khan, from whom khans and sultans were traditionally drawn—and the qoja, who held religious
prestige through claimed descent from Islamic religious lineages. The category should not be understood simply as a wealthy
class: its basis was associated with lineage and recognised social status.
sections.Social function:
The distinction helped organise social rank and political legitimacy. In particular, Chinggisid descent was historically important
for eligibility to the khanly position. The social category also shaped relationships between aristocratic lineages and the wider
population.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include lineage, political legitimacy, inherited status, and social hierarchy. A modern explanation should
make clear that this was a historical social classification, not a statement about the value or abilities of people based on
ancestry.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Ақсүйек әулеті — an aristocratic lineage.
     ●​   Ақсүйектер тобы — the aristocratic social group.
     ●​   Ақсүйек пен қарасүйек — the aristocratic and commoner categories.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Aristocracy: The most useful broad equivalent.
     ●​   Noble lineage: Appropriate when descent is central.
      ●​   Hereditary elite: Useful for explaining inherited status, but may imply wealth or political power in every case.
     ●​   White-bone class: A literal translation that requires explanation.
     ●​   Aqsúiek: Best retained in historical discussion.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Aqsúiek literally means “white bone” and refers to a historically recognised aristocratic category in Kazakh society. It was
associated especially with lineages claiming descent from Chinggis Khan and with certain religiously prestigious lineages. The
category was not simply a group of rich people: its status was connected with ancestry and traditional social hierarchy. The term
is often contrasted with qarasúiek, a category covering the wider population outside the aristocratic lineages. For international
readers, it is important to understand aqsúiek as a historical classification rather than a modern social or biological category.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Dauytbekova, M., & Zharylgasynova, B. (2018). “From the History of State Institutions of Governance of the Kazakh
          Khanate.” Journal of History, 90(3), 209–219. Article
     ●​   Dauytbekova, M. (2017). “From the History of Potestarion-Political Institutes of the Kazakh People.” Article
     ●​   Supports: The historical political structure and role of elite lineages and political institutions.
     ●​   Verification status: Draft. A specialist historical or ethnographic source explicitly defining aqsúiek, töre, and qoja is
          required before final publication.

heading: Qarasúiek

category.title: Historical, Social and National Concepts
category.description: Institutions, identities and ideas from Kazakh history and society.

short: Qarasúiek literally means “black bone.” Historically, it referred broadly to the commoner population in contrast with the aqsúiek aristocratic category.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Қарасүйек
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Qarasúiek
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /qɑrɑˈsʊjek/
     ●​   Word class: Noun; historical social-category term.
     ●​   Related forms: Қара (qara, black; also used in several social and symbolic expressions); сүйек (súiek, bone);
          ақсүйек (aqsúiek, aristocratic category).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Qarasúiek literally means “black bone.” Historically, it referred broadly to the commoner population in contrast with the aqsúiek
aristocratic category. It did not necessarily mean poverty or low personal worth.
sections.Cultural context:
In traditional Kazakh social classification, qarasúiek included the wider population outside the aristocratic lineages associated
with Chinggisid descent and certain religiously prestigious groups. Members of this category could hold considerable influence
as biys, batyrs, wealthy pastoralists, or community leaders. Therefore, the distinction between aqsúiek and qarasúiek should
not be confused with a simple division between powerful and powerless people.
sections.Social function:
The term helped distinguish hereditary aristocratic status from the broader population. It is useful for understanding historical
social hierarchy, political legitimacy, and the different bases of authority in traditional society.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include social belonging, non-aristocratic status, and the structure of historical hierarchy. The term should
not be interpreted as an insult or as a judgement about a person's character, intelligence, wealth, or dignity.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Қарасүйек қауымы — the commoner population.
     ●​   Ақсүйек пен қарасүйек — aristocratic and commoner social categories.
     ●​   Қарасүйектен шыққан би — a biy from a non-aristocratic background.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Commoner: The clearest general equivalent.
     ●​   Non-aristocratic population: More precise in historical writing.
     ●​   Commoner class: Useful when discussing social classification.
     ●​   Black-bone class: Literal, but requires cultural explanation.
     ●​   Qarasúiek: Best retained when discussing the historical Kazakh social system.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Qarasúiek literally means “black bone” and was a historical term for the wider population outside the aristocratic category
known as aqsúiek. It is important not to translate it as “poor people” or “lower class.” A person from a qarasúiek background
could become influential through reputation, wealth, knowledge, military leadership, or service to the community. The distinction
primarily concerned recognised lineage and traditional social status. It therefore helps explain how hereditary rank and earned
authority could coexist within Kazakh society.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Dauytbekova, M., & Zharylgasynova, B. (2018). “From the History of State Institutions of Governance of the Kazakh
          Khanate.” Journal of History, 90(3), 209–219. Article
     ●​   Dauytbekova, M. (2017). “From the History of Potestarion-Political Institutes of the Kazakh People.” Article
     ●​   Supports: The traditional political and social structure of Kazakh society.
     ●​   Verification status: Draft. A specialised source directly defining the aqsúiek–qarasúiek distinction and its internal
          diversity is required.

heading: Alash

category.title: Historical, Social and National Concepts
category.description: Institutions, identities and ideas from Kazakh history and society.

short: Alash is a historical and symbolic name associated with Kazakh collective identity.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Алаш
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Alash
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /ɑˈlɑʃ/
     ●​   Word class: Proper noun; historical and symbolic ethnopolitical term.
     ●​   Related forms: Алаш жұрты (Alash jurty, the people of Alash); Алаш қозғалысы (Alash qoǵalysy, the Alash
          movement); Алаш Орда (Alash Orda, the Alash government); Алаш партиясы (Alash partiyasy, the Alash Party).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Alash is a historical and symbolic name associated with Kazakh collective identity. In different contexts, it can refer to an
ancestral or legendary collective, the Kazakh people, or the early twentieth-century national movement known as the Alash
movement.
sections.Cultural context:
The term gained particular political importance in the early twentieth century. The Alash movement was led by Kazakh
intellectuals who sought political autonomy, modernisation, education, and the protection of the interests of the Kazakh
population within the changing political conditions of the Russian Empire and the revolutionary period. The movement
established the Alash Party and the Alash Orda government. The name also drew on ideas of common ancestry and collective
identity. The historical movement and the older symbolic use of the word should not be treated as identical.
sections.Social function:
Alash has functioned as a symbol of collective identity, political mobilisation, national consciousness, and historical memory. In
modern discourse, it is often used when discussing the intellectual heritage of the early twentieth-century national movement.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include unity, education, self-government, national dignity, political autonomy, and public responsibility.
Interpretations of Alash have changed across historical periods and political narratives, so the term should not be reduced to
one timeless or uncontested meaning.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Алаш қозғалысы — the Alash movement.
     ●​   Алаш Орда үкіметі — the Alash Orda government.
     ●​   Алаш зиялылары — the Alash intelligentsia.
     ●​   Алаш идеясы — the Alash idea / the idea associated with Alash.
     ●​   Алаш мұрасы — the heritage of Alash.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Alash: The original proper name; retain it.
     ●​   The Alash movement: The standard English description of the early twentieth-century political movement.
     ●​   Kazakh national movement: Useful as an explanation, but too broad to replace the name.
     ●​   Ancestral collective: Appropriate only when discussing the older symbolic or legendary meaning.
     ●​   Alash Orda: Retain as the historical name of the political organisation/government.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Alash is a historically significant name connected with Kazakh collective identity and political thought. It has older symbolic
associations with common ancestry and the unity of the Kazakh people. In the early twentieth century, it became the name of a
national movement led by educated Kazakh intellectuals who sought political autonomy, social modernisation, educational
development, and the protection of the population's interests. The movement established the Alash Party and the Alash Orda
government during the revolutionary period. For international readers, it is important to distinguish the older symbolic meaning
of Alash from the specific political movement of the 1910s. The two are related, but they are not interchangeable.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Kesici, Ö. (2017). “The Alash Movement and the Question of Kazakh Ethnicity.” Nationalities Papers, 45(6),
          1135–1149. Article
     ●​   Saktaganova, Z. G., Omarova, B. K., Ilyassova, K. M., Nurligenova, Z. N., Abzhapparova, B. Zh., Zhalmurzina, A.
          Zh., & Mazhitova, Zh. S. (2020). “The Alash Party: Historiography of the Movement.” Repository record
     ●​   Arynov, Zh. M., & Alibekov, S. B. (2022). “The National Idea of the Alash Movement.” Journal of History, 105(2),
          210–215. Article
     ●​   Supports: The early twentieth-century Alash movement, its political programme, national identity discourse, and
          historical significance.
     ●​   Verification status: Source identified and directly relevant. The older legendary etymology and the relationship
          between Alash as a symbolic name and the three zhuzes require separate specialist evidence.

VI. Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
— 86–93
The entries below are written in English for an international audience. They distinguish linguistic meaning from cultural
interpretation and avoid presenting Islamic, Turkic, or broader human concepts as exclusively Kazakh. The transliteration is a
practical Latin rendering; it should eventually be standardised across all 100 cards.

heading: JAN

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Jan refers to the soul, life, or a person's inner being.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Жан
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Jan
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /ʒɑn/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Жанды (jandy, living/alive); жансыз (jansyz, lifeless); жан дүниесі (jan düniesi, inner world);
          жанашыр (janashyr, caring/supportive person).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Jan refers to the soul, life, or a person's inner being. Depending on context, it can describe the spiritual dimension of a person,
the principle of life, or a person themselves. It also appears in affectionate forms of address and expressions of emotional
closeness.
sections.Cultural context:
The concept has several layers shaped by everyday Kazakh language, Turkic cultural heritage, and Islamic thought. In religious
contexts, jan may refer to the soul, while in ordinary speech it can mean life, a person, or one's emotional inner world. These
meanings should not be reduced to one fixed theological definition.
sections.Social function:
Jan appears in expressions of affection, compassion, grief, and concern for another person's well-being. It allows speakers to
describe human life and emotional experience in personal rather than purely physical terms.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include life, humanity, compassion, emotional depth, and spiritual existence. However, the word does not
always carry a religious meaning; its interpretation depends on the expression and situation.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Жан дүниесі — one's inner world.
     ●​   Жаным — my dear / my soul (an affectionate form of address).
     ●​   Жан сақтау — to preserve one's life / survive.
     ●​   Жаны ашу — to feel compassion for someone.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Soul: Best in spiritual or religious contexts.
     ●​   Life: Appropriate when the word refers to the principle or condition of being alive.
     ●​   Inner self: Useful when describing a person's emotional and psychological world.
     ●​   Person: Possible in some expressions, but it loses the spiritual and emotional associations.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Jan is a flexible Kazakh word that connects ideas of life, the soul, and a person's inner world. In a religious conversation, it may
refer to the soul as a spiritual dimension of human existence. In everyday speech, however, it can appear in affectionate
expressions or descriptions of emotional experience. For example, жан дүниесі refers to a person's inner world, while жаным
can be used as a term of affection. Translating every occurrence as “soul” would therefore be misleading. International readers
should interpret the word through its surrounding expression and context.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Gabitkhanuly, K., & Sabyr, M. (2025). “Religious Terminological Concepts – Reflection of Islamic and Traditional
          Kazakh Worldview in Language.” Eurasian Journal of Philology: Science and Education, 199(3), 42–54. Article record
     ●​   Akhmetzhanova, Z. K. (2012). Очерки по национальной концептологии. Repository record
     ●​   Supports: The broader relationship between language, worldview, and religious-cultural concepts. These sources
          should not be treated as direct verification of every meaning or example above.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A dedicated dictionary or linguistic study of жан and its semantic range is still
          required.

heading: RUKH

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Rukh refers to spirit, spiritual strength, or an inner source of motivation and identity.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Рух
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Rukh
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /rʊx/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Рухани (rukhani, spiritual); рухтану (rukhtanu, to become inspired or encouraged); рухты (rukhty,
          spirited / having strong morale).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Rukh refers to spirit, spiritual strength, or an inner source of motivation and identity. Depending on context, it can describe
spirituality, courage, morale, or the collective spirit of a community.
sections.Cultural context:
The word has connections to Arabic-derived religious vocabulary and has developed broader meanings in Kazakh intellectual,
cultural, and public discourse. In religious contexts, it can refer to the spirit. In national and cultural discussions, it may describe
collective morale, historical consciousness, or cultural vitality. These uses are related but not identical.
sections.Social function:
Rukh is used to express and strengthen a sense of shared identity, resilience, and purpose. It appears in discussions of
education, cultural heritage, national development, and personal motivation.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include spiritual depth, courage, resilience, dignity, and cultural continuity. Nevertheless, rukh should not
automatically be equated with patriotism or national identity; it also has personal and religious meanings.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Ұлттық рух — national spirit.
     ●​   Рухани даму — spiritual development.
     ●​   Рухы биік — high-spirited / possessing strong morale.
     ●​   Рухтану — to become inspired or encouraged.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Spirit: The broadest and most flexible equivalent.
     ●​   Spirituality: Appropriate when the religious or inner-development dimension is central.
     ●​   Morale: Best when referring to the confidence and determination of a group.
     ●​   Cultural spirit: Useful when discussing shared identity and cultural continuity.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Rukh can describe something deeper than temporary enthusiasm. It may refer to a person's spiritual orientation, the strength
that helps someone endure difficulties, or the shared identity of a community. The expression ұлттық рух is often translated as
“national spirit,” particularly in discussions of history, culture, and collective identity. By contrast, рухани даму refers to spiritual
or inner development. The correct English equivalent therefore depends on whether the context is religious, personal, cultural,
or collective. It is important not to assume that every use of rukh has a religious meaning.
sections.Evidence:
●​    Gabitkhanuly, K., & Sabyr, M. (2025). “Religious Terminological Concepts – Reflection of Islamic and Traditional
           Kazakh Worldview in Language.” Article record
     ●​    Smagulova, G. N., & Makataeva, Sh. M. (2020). “Лингвоаксиология: қазақтар дүниетанымындағы құндылықтар
           ұғымы.” KazNU Bulletin. Philology Series, 177(1), 187–193. Article record
     ●​    Supports: The study of religious and value-related concepts in Kazakh linguistic worldview.
     ●​    Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialised source distinguishing religious, psychological, and national uses of
           рух is needed.

heading: TAGDYR

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Tagdyr means fate or destiny: the course of events and circumstances that shape a person's life.

sections.Identification:
●​    Kazakh: Тағдыр
     ●​    Latin transliteration: Tagdyr
     ●​    Pronunciation (IPA): /tɑɣˈdɯr/ (approximate)
     ●​    Word class: Noun
     ●​    Related forms: Тағдырлас (tagdyr las, sharing a similar fate); тағдырлы (tagdy rly, significant or fateful); тағдыр
           шешу (tagdyr sheshu, to determine someone's fate).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Tagdyr means fate or destiny: the course of events and circumstances that shape a person's life. It may refer to events
perceived as beyond individual control, or to the overall direction and outcome of a person's life.
sections.Cultural context:
The concept is important in religious, philosophical, and everyday discourse. In Islamic contexts, discussions of fate may relate
to divine decree, while everyday usage can refer more broadly to life's circumstances and uncertainty. The word should not be
interpreted as proof that Kazakh culture promotes passive acceptance of events.
sections.Social function:
Tagdyr provides a way to discuss difficult experiences, unexpected events, personal circumstances, and the limits of human
control. It can also express sympathy when people face hardship.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include acceptance, patience, humility, uncertainty, and reflection on human limitations. At the same time,
people may discuss fate while emphasising personal responsibility and the ability to make choices.
sections.Practical application:
●​    Адам тағдыры — a person's fate / life story.
     ●​    Тағдыр жазуы — what fate has determined.
     ●​    Тағдыр тәлкегі — the twists of fate.
      ●​   Тағдырлас адамдар — people who share a similar fate.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Fate: Best for circumstances or events perceived as outside personal control.
     ●​   Destiny: Often suggests a predetermined direction or significant purpose.
     ●​   Fortune: Appropriate in some contexts involving luck, but not a general equivalent.
     ●​   Life story: Useful when the word refers to the course of someone's life rather than predestination.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Tagdyr is used to speak about the course of human life, especially circumstances that a person cannot fully control. It may
appear in religious discussions about divine decree, but it is also common in ordinary conversations about hardship,
relationships, and unexpected events. For example, адам тағдыры can refer to a person's life and the circumstances that
shape it. Translating the word as “destiny” in every situation may suggest a fixed purpose that is not necessarily present in the
Kazakh expression. A careful translation should distinguish religious belief, perceived inevitability, and the broader idea of a
person's life course.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Khamzina, M. B. (2026). “Semantic Evolution of Religious Vocabulary in Kazakh Language: Linguocognitive and
          Corpus Interpretation.” Article record
     ●​   Supports: The treatment of тағдыр within research on religious vocabulary and its semantic development in Kazakh.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. The article is relevant to the religious and linguistic dimension; a dedicated study
          of everyday usage and philosophical interpretations is still needed.

heading: NESIBE

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Nesibe refers to one's allotted share, provision, or portion of what life offers.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Несібе
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Nesibe
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /nʲeˈsʲɪˌbʲe/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Несібесін көру (nesibesin köru, to receive one's share or portion); несібелі (nesibeli, fortunate /
          blessed with one's share); несібе бұйыру (nesibe buiyru, for a share or opportunity to be granted).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Nesibe refers to one's allotted share, provision, or portion of what life offers. It can describe food, livelihood, opportunity, or a
person's share of good fortune. In religious contexts, it may carry the sense of provision granted by God.
sections.Cultural context:
The word is associated with religious vocabulary and everyday expressions about livelihood, provision, and what a person
receives in life. Its meaning can overlap with ideas of fate and divine provision, but nesibe is more specifically concerned with
one's share or provision rather than the entire course of life.
sections.Social function:
Nesibe can express acceptance, gratitude, and recognition that people receive different opportunities or portions in life. It is also
used when sharing food or discussing livelihood and good fortune.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include gratitude, provision, humility, and acceptance. However, the concept should not be interpreted as
a reason to reject effort or personal responsibility.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Несібем осы екен — this is what I have been allotted / this is my share.
     ●​   Несібесін табу — to earn one's living / find one's provision.
     ●​   Несібесі мол — well provided for / fortunate.
     ●​   Несібесі бұйырды — it became their share / it was granted to them.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Share: Best when referring to an allotted portion.
     ●​   Provision: Appropriate for livelihood or sustenance, especially in religious contexts.
     ●​   Fortune: Useful when the emphasis is on good luck or favourable circumstances.
     ●​   Destined portion: Can explain the idea, but sounds unnatural in many ordinary English sentences.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Nesibe describes the portion of life, livelihood, or opportunity that a person receives. It is often used in expressions that
combine acceptance with gratitude. For example, someone may refer to food or an opportunity as their nesibe, suggesting that
it has become their share. In religious contexts, the word may imply that provision comes from God. However, it does not simply
mean “fate”: tagdyr refers more broadly to the course of a person's life, while nesibe focuses on the share or provision received.
English translations such as “share,” “provision,” or “fortune” should be selected according to context.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Khamzina, M. B. (2026). “Semantic Evolution of Religious Vocabulary in Kazakh Language: Linguocognitive and
          Corpus Interpretation.” Article record
     ●​   Supports: The broader analysis of religious vocabulary and related worldview concepts in Kazakh.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A direct lexical study of несібе and its collocations is required before treating the
          examples as fully verified.

heading: NAPSI

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Napsi refers to the self, ego, or the human drive for personal desires and appetites.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Нәпсі
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Napsi
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /næpˈsɯ/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Нәпсіқұмар (napsiqumar, driven by desires); нәпсісін тыю (napsisin tyiu, to restrain one's desires);
          нәпсіге берілу (napsige berilu, to give in to one's desires).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Napsi refers to the self, ego, or the human drive for personal desires and appetites. In Islamic moral and spiritual discourse, it
often describes the part of human nature associated with desires that require discipline and self-control.
sections.Cultural context:
The term comes from Arabic-derived religious vocabulary and is used in Islamic ethical and spiritual discussions. In this
context, napsi is not simply the existence of human needs or desires; it can refer to the struggle to control impulses that conflict
with moral or spiritual responsibilities. Its meaning varies according to the religious and everyday context.
sections.Social function:
Napsi provides a vocabulary for discussing self-discipline, temptation, greed, selfishness, and moral responsibility. It can be
used to encourage reflection on whether a person's actions are guided by considered values or immediate desires.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include self-restraint, discipline, humility, moral awareness, and spiritual development. It should not be
interpreted as meaning that all desires are inherently bad or that human needs should be suppressed.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Нәпсісін тыю — to restrain one's desires.
     ●​   Нәпсіге берілу — to give in to one's desires.
     ●​   Нәпсіқұмарлық — excessive desire / self-indulgence.
     ●​   Нәпсіні тәрбиелеу — to discipline or cultivate the self.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Ego: Useful in some contexts, but may suggest a psychological concept rather than a religious one.
     ●​   Desire: Appropriate for the drive or appetite being discussed.
     ●​   Lower self: Useful in Islamic ethical contexts, although it requires explanation.
     ●​   Self-indulgence: Best when the emphasis is on excessive personal gratification.
     ●​   Carnal desire: Appropriate only when physical or sensual appetite is specifically intended.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Napsi is an important term in Islamic moral vocabulary. It is often used to discuss the human tendency to follow immediate
desires, seek excessive pleasure, or act selfishly. Expressions such as нәпсісін тыю describe the effort to control these
impulses. The concept is not identical to the English word “ego,” because it can carry a religious and ethical meaning that goes
beyond self-image or personal identity. Nor does it mean that every human desire is wrong. In many contexts, the central issue
is whether a person can regulate desires and act in accordance with moral responsibilities.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Gabitkhanuly, K., & Sabyr, M. (2025). “Religious Terminological Concepts – Reflection of Islamic and Traditional
          Kazakh Worldview in Language.” Article record
     ●​   Khamzina, M. B. (2026). “Semantic Evolution of Religious Vocabulary in Kazakh Language: Linguocognitive and
          Corpus Interpretation.” Article record
     ●​   Supports: The role of Islamic and religious vocabulary in Kazakh linguistic worldview; Khamzina's study explicitly
          includes нәпсі among the terms investigated.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialised Islamic theological source would strengthen the explanation of the
          term's ethical and spiritual meanings.

heading: QUDAIY QONAQ

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Qudaiy qonaq refers to an unexpected or passing guest who arrives without a prior invitation.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Құдайы қонақ
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Qudaiy qonaq
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /qʊˈdɑjɯ qɔˈnɑq/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun phrase
     ●​   Components: Құдайы (qudaiy, belonging to or associated with God); қонақ (qonaq, guest).
     ●​   Related forms: Қонақжайлық (qonaqzhailyq, hospitality); қонақасы (qonaqasy, a meal served to a guest).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Qudaiy qonaq refers to an unexpected or passing guest who arrives without a prior invitation. The expression carries the idea
that such a guest should be received with hospitality rather than treated as an inconvenience.
sections.Cultural context:
The expression is associated with Kazakh hospitality and the moral importance of receiving travellers and unexpected visitors.
The word qudaiy gives the phrase a religious or sacred association, but the expression should not be reduced to a formal
religious rule. Its cultural meaning is connected to the expectation that a guest deserves respectful treatment.
sections.Social function:
The concept encourages people to receive unexpected visitors, offer food or rest where possible, and maintain social goodwill.
It can also express an expectation that hospitality should extend beyond close friends and relatives.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include generosity, kindness, respect for guests, and responsibility towards travellers. However, the
expression describes a cultural ideal and should not be used to claim that every household can always provide accommodation
or extensive hospitality.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Құдайы қонақ келді — an unexpected guest has arrived.
     ●​   Құдайы қонаққа қонақасы беру — to provide a meal for an unexpected guest.
     ●​   Құдайы қонақпын — I am a passing / unexpected guest.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Unexpected guest: The clearest neutral translation.
     ●​   Passing traveller: Useful when the person is travelling and stops by.
     ●​   Guest sent by God: Communicates the religious imagery, but may sound overly literal.
     ●​   Uninvited guest: Sometimes accurate, but can sound negative or unwelcome in English.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Qudaiy qonaq is an expression associated with the Kazakh ideal of hospitality. It refers to someone who arrives unexpectedly,
often while travelling or passing through. The phrase suggests that a guest should be treated with kindness even when the visit
has not been arranged in advance. The word qudaiy literally connects the guest with God, giving the expression a moral and
religious dimension. However, “uninvited guest” is not always a good translation because it can suggest that the visitor is
unwanted. “Unexpected guest” or “passing traveller” usually communicates the social meaning more clearly. The phrase
expresses a cultural expectation, not a universal description of how every household behaves.
sections.Evidence:
●​   “Linguocultural Characteristics of Guest Hosting Traditions of Kazakh and Turkish People.” Research PDF
     ●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General context of Kazakh hospitality and guest-reception practices. Neither source has been confirmed
          here as a direct lexical study of the exact phrase.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A source explicitly documenting құдайы қонақ and its customary interpretation is
          still needed.

heading: DUNIE

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Dunie has several related meanings: the world, worldly life, material possessions, or the affairs of human existence.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Дүние
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Dunie
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /dʏˈnʲe/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Дүниетаным (dunietanym, worldview); дүниеге келу (duniege kelu, to be born); дүниеден өту
          (dunieden ötu, to pass away); дүниеқоңыз (dunieq ońyz, greedy / materialistic).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Dunie has several related meanings: the world, worldly life, material possessions, or the affairs of human existence. In religious
and philosophical contexts, it can refer specifically to temporary earthly life in contrast with the afterlife.
sections.Cultural context:
The word is used in everyday Kazakh speech as well as philosophical and religious discourse. In Islamic contexts, dunie can
describe the temporary material world, often contrasted with aqiret (the afterlife). In ordinary usage, it can simply mean the
world, life, or possessions. Its interpretation therefore depends heavily on context.
sections.Social function:
Dunie provides a way to discuss material wealth, the temporary nature of life, human priorities, and the relationship between
worldly concerns and spiritual responsibilities.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include impermanence, moderation, responsibility, and reflection on material desires. However, the word
does not always carry a negative meaning: it can refer neutrally to the world or to everyday life.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Бұл дүние — this world / this life.
     ●​   Дүниеге келу — to be born.
     ●​   Дүниеден өту — to pass away.
     ●​   Дүние-мүлік — property and possessions.
     ●​   Дүниеге қызығу — to be attracted to worldly things.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   World: Best for the general world or human environment.
     ●​   Worldly life: Appropriate in religious or philosophical contexts.
     ●​   Possessions: Useful when the word refers to material property.
     ●​   Life: Appropriate in expressions about birth, death, and human existence.
     ●​   Material world: Useful when contrasting earthly existence with spiritual or afterlife concerns.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Dunie is a broad word that can refer to the world, human life, or material possessions. In everyday expressions, it may have a
neutral meaning. For example, дүниеге келу means “to be born,” while дүние-мүлік refers to property and possessions. In
religious discourse, however, дunia may refer to temporary earthly existence, which is often contrasted with the afterlife. This
distinction matters because translating every occurrence as “worldly possessions” or “materialism” would distort the meaning.
International readers should pay attention to the expression in which the word appears and whether the speaker is discussing
ordinary life, wealth, or spiritual ideas.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Gabitkhanuly, K., & Sabyr, M. (2025). “Religious Terminological Concepts – Reflection of Islamic and Traditional
          Kazakh Worldview in Language.” Article record
      ●​   Akhmetzhanova, Z. K. (2012). Очерки по национальной концептологии. Repository record
     ●​   Supports: General research frameworks for religious and culturally significant concepts in Kazakh language.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A dedicated dictionary entry and corpus analysis are needed to verify the full
          range of meanings and examples.

heading: FANI MEN BAQI

category.title: Spiritual and Philosophical Concepts
category.description: Spiritual, religious and philosophical understandings.

short: Fani men baqi expresses a contrast between the temporary and the eternal.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Фәни мен бақи
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Fani men baqi
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /fæˈnɪ mʲen bɑˈqɯ/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Coordinated noun phrase
     ●​   Components: Фәни (fani, transient / temporary); бақи (baqi, eternal / everlasting); мен (men, and).
     ●​   Related forms: Фәни дүние (fani dunie, transient earthly world); бақи дүние (baqi dunie, eternal world / afterlife).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Fani men baqi expresses a contrast between the temporary and the eternal. In Islamic religious discourse, fani refers to the
transient earthly world and baqi to eternal existence, particularly the afterlife.
sections.Cultural context:
The expression belongs to a religious and philosophical vocabulary influenced by Islamic thought. It is used to reflect on
mortality, the temporary nature of worldly life, and the belief in an eternal afterlife. The contrast also appears in broader moral
reflections about what is temporary and what is lasting.
sections.Social function:
The expression can encourage reflection on mortality, ethical conduct, spiritual priorities, and the consequences of human
actions. It is used in religious teaching, philosophical discussion, and conversations about the meaning of life.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include humility, spiritual responsibility, awareness of mortality, and the distinction between temporary
possessions and lasting moral or spiritual significance. Its meaning should be presented as a religious-philosophical framework
rather than as a belief shared by every Kazakh person.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Фәни дүние — the transient earthly world.
     ●​   Бақи дүние — the eternal world / the afterlife.
     ●​   Фәни мен бақиды ойлау — to reflect on the temporary and the eternal.
     ●​   Бұл дүние — фәни — this world is temporary.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   The transient and the eternal: The clearest conceptual translation.
     ●​   The temporal world and the afterlife: Best when the religious contrast is central.
     ●​   Mortal life and eternal existence: Useful in philosophical explanations.
     ●​   The temporary and the everlasting: Accessible to general readers, although less explicitly religious.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Fani men baqi expresses a contrast between two ways of understanding existence: the temporary nature of earthly life and the
idea of eternal life after death. In Islamic thought, fani refers to the world that eventually passes away, while baqi refers to what
remains eternal. The expression can therefore be used to remind people that wealth, status, and physical life are temporary,
while spiritual and moral responsibilities have a different significance. It is not simply a contrast between “life” and “death.” It
reflects a religious understanding of mortality and the afterlife. When introducing this concept to international readers, it is
important to explain its Islamic background rather than present it as a belief held uniformly by all Kazakh people.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Gabitkhanuly, K., & Sabyr, M. (2025). “Religious Terminological Concepts – Reflection of Islamic and Traditional
          Kazakh Worldview in Language.” Article record
     ●​   Khamzina, M. B. (2026). “Semantic Evolution of Religious Vocabulary in Kazakh Language: Linguocognitive and
          Corpus Interpretation.” Article record
     ●​   Supports: The broader role of Islamic vocabulary and religious concepts in Kazakh linguistic worldview. Direct
          verification of this exact paired expression remains necessary.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A dedicated source on the theological distinction between fani and baqi in
          Kazakh religious discourse is required.

VII. Material Culture and Traditional
Lifestyle — 94–100

heading: KIIZ UI

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Kiiz ui literally means “felt house.” It refers to the traditional portable dwelling used by Kazakh communities and other peoples of Central Asia.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Киіз үй
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Kiiz ui
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /kʲiˈzʊj/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun phrase
     ●​   Components: Киіз (kiiz, felt); үй (ui, house).
     ●​   Related terms: Шаңырақ (shańyraq, circular crown of the yurt); уық (uyq, roof poles); кереге (kerege, lattice wall);
          есік (esik, door); туырлық (tu y rlyq, felt wall covering); үзік (üzik, felt roof covering).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Kiiz ui literally means “felt house.” It refers to the traditional portable dwelling used by Kazakh communities and other peoples of
Central Asia. Its structure typically consists of a collapsible lattice wall, roof poles, a circular crown, and felt coverings.
sections.Cultural context:
The yurt developed as a practical dwelling suited to mobile pastoral life. Its portable structure made it possible to assemble,
dismantle, and transport a household's living space as people moved with their livestock. It also became an important symbol of
Kazakh cultural heritage. However, it should not be presented as an exclusively Kazakh invention: related forms of felt-covered
portable dwellings have been used across Central Asia and the Eurasian steppe.
sections.Social function:
The kiiz ui served as a family home and a place for receiving guests, preparing food, conducting household activities, and
holding important social gatherings. Its interior arrangement could reflect social relationships, hospitality practices, and
distinctions between different areas of the household.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include mobility, adaptation to the environment, family life, hospitality, craftsmanship, and continuity
between generations. Its symbolic meaning should not obscure its practical function as a dwelling designed for particular
environmental and economic conditions.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Киіз үй тігу — to erect or assemble a yurt.
     ●​   Киіз үйді жинау — to dismantle a yurt.
     ●​   Киіз үйдің керегесі — the lattice wall of a yurt.
     ●​   Киіз үйдің шаңырағы — the circular crown of a yurt.
     ●​   Киіз үйде қонақ күту — to receive guests in a yurt.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Yurt: The established English term and the most practical translation.
     ●​   Felt dwelling: A descriptive translation that explains the material and function.
     ●​   Traditional Kazakh dwelling: Useful when the cultural context is specifically Kazakh.
     ●​   Nomadic tent: Too broad and potentially misleading; a yurt has a distinct structural design and is not simply a tent.
sections.Cultural transfer:
The kiiz ui, commonly called a yurt in English, is a portable dwelling traditionally associated with mobile pastoral communities of
the Kazakh steppe. Its structure is designed to be assembled and dismantled: a lattice framework forms the walls, poles
support the roof, and felt coverings protect the interior. This design made the dwelling suitable for communities whose seasonal
movements were connected to livestock and pasture. The yurt was also a household and social space, not merely temporary
shelter. Families used it for everyday life and for receiving visitors. Its interior organisation could communicate relationships and
customary distinctions between spaces. Although the yurt is a major symbol of Kazakh heritage, similar structures are found
among other Central Asian and steppe peoples.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General background on Kazakh traditional customs and material culture. It should not be treated as
          sufficient technical documentation of every structural component.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialist ethnographic or architectural source on the construction, regional
          forms, and interior organisation of the Kazakh yurt is required.

heading: SHAŃYRAQ

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Shańyraq is the circular wooden crown at the top of a traditional Kazakh yurt.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Шаңырақ
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Shańyraq
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /ʃɑˈŋɯˌrɑq/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Шаңырақ көтеру (shańyraq köteru, to raise a yurt's crown; figuratively, to establish a household);
          қара шаңырақ (qara shańyraq, the ancestral family home); шаңырағы биік болсын (shańyraǵy biik bolsyn, may your
          household prosper).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Shańyraq is the circular wooden crown at the top of a traditional Kazakh yurt. It connects the roof poles and forms the upper
opening of the dwelling. In figurative usage, it can represent a household, family continuity, or the home as a shared centre of
family life.
sections.Cultural context:
The shańyraq is an important structural and symbolic element of the yurt. Because it occupies the upper central part of the
dwelling and connects its roof structure, it has acquired meanings associated with family unity and continuity. The expression
қара шаңырақ is commonly associated with the ancestral family home, although its precise social implications should be
explained through family customs and regional context rather than assumed to be identical in every household.
sections.Social function:
The word is used in discussions of marriage, family establishment, inheritance, and intergenerational continuity. The expression
шаңырақ көтеру can refer to starting a new household, while қара шаңырақ can identify the family home associated with
previous generations.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include family unity, continuity, responsibility, belonging, and respect for ancestors. The symbolism should
not be reduced to the idea that every family follows one identical inheritance or household structure.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Шаңырақ көтеру — to establish a household / start a family.
     ●​   Қара шаңырақ — the ancestral family home.
     ●​   Шаңырағы биік болсын — may your household prosper.
     ●​   Шаңырақтың астында — under the same household roof.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Yurt crown: The precise literal translation of the architectural element.
     ●​   Household: Appropriate in figurative expressions referring to family life.
     ●​   Ancestral home: Useful for қара шаңырақ, though it may not capture every customary implication.
     ●​   Family lineage: Sometimes relevant, but too broad to serve as a direct translation.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Shańyraq has both a physical and a symbolic meaning. Literally, it is the circular wooden crown at the top of a Kazakh yurt,
where the roof poles meet. In cultural language, it can represent the household and the continuity of family life. The expression
шаңырақ көтеру is used when a new household is established, while қара шаңырақ refers to the ancestral family home. These
expressions show how an architectural feature can become a way of speaking about family relationships and continuity.
Translating shańyraq simply as “roof” would miss its specific structure and symbolic role. In an international explanation, it is
useful to introduce the physical object first and then explain its figurative meanings.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Akhmetzhanova, Z. K. (2012). Очерки по национальной концептологии. Repository record
     ●​   Supports: General research context for Kazakh cultural concepts and traditional practices. These references do not,
          by themselves, verify all the architectural and figurative details above.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A dedicated ethnographic source on the shańyraq and the customary meaning
          of қара шаңырақ is needed.

heading: DOMBYRA

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Dombyra is the name of a traditional Kazakh plucked string instrument.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Домбыра
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Dombyra
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /dɔmˈbɯˌrɑ/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related terms: Күй (küy, instrumental composition); домбырашы (dombyrashy, dombyra player); домбыра тарту
          (dombyra tartu, to play the dombyra); домбыра күйлері (dombyra küileri, dombyra instrumental compositions).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Dombyra is the name of a traditional Kazakh plucked string instrument. The most familiar form has a long neck, a hollow body,
and usually two strings. It is played by plucking or striking the strings with the fingers.
sections.Cultural context:
The dombyra is closely associated with Kazakh musical traditions, especially the performance of küy. It has been used in solo
performance, musical storytelling, and the transmission of historical and cultural memory. Instrument design, playing technique,
and musical repertoire vary across regions and performance traditions. Similar long-necked plucked instruments exist in other
cultures, so the dombyra should be described as a major instrument of Kazakh musical heritage rather than as an instrument
with no regional relatives.
sections.Social function:
The dombyra accompanies musical performances, cultural celebrations, competitions, and informal gatherings. Skilled
performers use it to communicate musical narratives, emotions, and interpretations of events. It also plays a role in teaching
younger generations about traditional music.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include cultural memory, artistic skill, identity, creativity, and intergenerational learning. The instrument is
an important symbol of Kazakh music, but its meaning is not limited to national symbolism: it is also a musical instrument used
for artistic expression and entertainment.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Домбыра тарту — to play the dombyra.
     ●​   Домбыра үйрену — to learn to play the dombyra.
     ●​   Домбырашы — a dombyra player.
     ●​   Домбырамен күй орындау — to perform a küy on the dombyra.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Dombyra: The preferred translation because it preserves the instrument's cultural identity.
     ●​   Kazakh two-stringed lute: A useful explanatory description for readers unfamiliar with the instrument.
     ●​   Plucked string instrument: Technically descriptive but too general.
     ●​   Traditional Kazakh instrument: Useful in introductory explanations, but not a complete definition.
sections.Cultural transfer:
The dombyra is one of the most recognisable instruments in Kazakh musical culture. It is a plucked string instrument, most
commonly with two strings, and is frequently used to perform küy—instrumental compositions that can communicate moods,
stories, and interpretations of events without words. The instrument is associated with both professional performers and
informal musical traditions. It is also important in cultural education, where people learn to play it and become familiar with
traditional musical repertoires. For international readers, “dombyra” is preferable to replacing the name with “lute” or “guitar.”
Those comparisons may help explain how it is played, but they do not fully describe its construction, sound, repertoire, or
cultural associations.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General context of Kazakh traditional culture. It is not a specialist source on organology or the history of
          the dombyra.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialist musicological or ethnomusicological source is needed for instrument
          construction, regional variants, playing techniques, and historical development.

heading: KÜI

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Küy refers to a traditional instrumental musical composition, particularly within Kazakh music.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Күй
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Küy
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /kʏj/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Күйші (küishi, performer or composer of küi); күй тарту (küy tartu, to perform a küi); күйшілік өнер
          (küishilik öner, the art of performing küi).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Küy refers to a traditional instrumental musical composition, particularly within Kazakh music. It is commonly performed on the
dombyra, although other instruments, including the kobyz, also have their own küy traditions. The word can also have broader
meanings related to mood, condition, or state in other contexts.
sections.Cultural context:
Küy occupies an important place in Kazakh instrumental music. Many compositions are associated with particular events,
landscapes, historical figures, personal experiences, or emotional states. Some have accompanying narratives explaining their
origins or meanings. Such stories should be treated carefully: the history of an individual composition may be documented,
transmitted through oral tradition, or disputed.
sections.Social function:
Küy is performed at cultural events, concerts, competitions, and informal gatherings. It allows musicians to communicate
without lyrics and provides a way to transmit musical traditions and collective memory. The performer may introduce a
composition through a short explanation or story.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include artistic expression, memory, emotional communication, musical knowledge, and cultural
continuity. However, not every küy represents a historical event or carries a single agreed narrative.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Күй тарту — to perform a küy.
     ●​   Күйші — a küy performer or composer.
     ●​   Домбыра күйі — a dombyra instrumental composition.
     ●​   Күй тыңдау — to listen to küy.
     ●​   Күйдің тарихы — the story or background of a küy.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Instrumental composition: The clearest explanatory translation.
     ●​   Traditional instrumental piece: Accessible and suitable for general readers.
     ●​   Musical narrative: Useful when a particular composition is associated with a story or historical event.
     ●​   Melody: Too narrow; it does not fully convey the form and cultural tradition.
      ●​   Tune: Too informal and general for most cultural explanations.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Küy is a traditional instrumental composition that holds a distinctive place in Kazakh music. It is often performed on the
dombyra and can also be associated with the kobyz and other instruments. Unlike a song with lyrics, a küy communicates
through melody, rhythm, performance technique, and musical development. Some compositions are connected with stories
about historical events, people, animals, or landscapes. These narratives can help listeners interpret the music, although not
every story has the same level of historical verification. The word should therefore not be translated simply as “song.”
“Traditional instrumental composition” is more accurate, while the original term küy preserves its particular place within Kazakh
musical culture.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General background on Kazakh cultural traditions. It does not provide sufficient specialist evidence for the
          musical form, repertoire, or individual composition histories.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A dedicated ethnomusicological source on küy, its genres, performance
          traditions, and oral narratives is required.

heading: KIIZ

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Kiiz means felt: a dense textile material traditionally produced by pressing and working wool fibres together.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Киіз
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Kiiz
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /kʲiˈz/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Киіз басу (kiiz basu, to make felt); киіз үй (kiiz ui, felt dwelling / yurt); текемет (tekemet, traditional
          decorative felt rug); сырмақ (syrmaq, stitched decorative felt rug).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Kiiz means felt: a dense textile material traditionally produced by pressing and working wool fibres together. Unlike woven
fabric, felt is made by matting fibres through moisture, heat, pressure, and friction.
sections.Cultural context:
Felt has been important in the material culture of Kazakh pastoral communities. Wool from livestock could be processed into a
durable material used for covering dwellings, making floor coverings, and producing household objects. Felt-making also
developed decorative techniques and regional styles. It is important to distinguish the general material kiiz from specific
products such as tekemet and syrmaq.
sections.Social function:
Felt production was part of household craft and material life. The preparation of wool and manufacture of felt objects could
involve shared work and the transmission of practical skills between generations. Felt products served domestic, protective,
and decorative purposes.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include craftsmanship, practical knowledge, adaptation to the environment, resourcefulness, and
continuity of household traditions. Felt should not be described only as a decorative cultural symbol: it was also a functional
material used in everyday life.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Киіз басу — to make felt.
     ●​   Киіз үй — a felt-covered yurt.
     ●​   Текемет жасау — to make a traditional felt rug.
     ●​   Киізден жасалған бұйым — an object made of felt.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Felt: The direct and most accurate English equivalent.
     ●​   Wool felt: Useful when the material's wool composition needs to be specified.
     ●​   Traditional felt textile: Appropriate in a cultural or museum context.
     ●​   Felt rug: Correct only when referring to a floor covering rather than the material itself.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Kiiz is a traditional felt material made by processing wool fibres until they form a dense textile. In Kazakh material culture, it has
been used for practical household purposes, particularly in the construction and covering of yurts. Felt has also been made into
decorative objects, including tekemet and syrmaq, which demonstrate different approaches to ornamentation and textile
craftsmanship. The word kiiz refers to the material itself, not to one particular object. This distinction is important: translating it
as “rug” would be inaccurate when the reference is to felt used in a yurt or another household product. For international
readers, the entry should explain both the production process and the different objects made from the material.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General background on traditional Kazakh material culture. It is not a technical study of felt production or
          textile terminology.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialist ethnographic or textile-history source is required to verify production
          methods, terminology, and distinctions between felt products.

heading: TÖR

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Tör refers to the place of honour in a traditional Kazakh home, generally located opposite the entrance.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Төр
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Tör
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /tœr/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Төрге шығу (törge shyǵu, to take a place of honour); төрлетіңіз (törletińiz, please come and take the
          place of honour); төр иесі (tör iesi, the person occupying or responsible for the place of honour, depending on
          context).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Tör refers to the place of honour in a traditional Kazakh home, generally located opposite the entrance. It is traditionally
associated with respected guests, elders, or people given special recognition. The word can also refer more broadly to an
honoured position or place.
sections.Cultural context:
The arrangement of space inside a traditional yurt had social significance. The tör, situated opposite the entrance, was
commonly regarded as the most honoured place. Offering someone this position could communicate respect and hospitality.
The exact seating arrangements could vary according to the household, occasion, and social context; they should not be
presented as an unchanging rule followed by every Kazakh family.
sections.Social function:
Tör helps organise social interaction during visits and gatherings. Inviting a guest to sit in the place of honour is a gesture of
respect. The expression can also be used metaphorically to describe a person's recognised position within a social setting.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include respect for guests, recognition of elders, hospitality, social dignity, and courtesy. However, the
practice should not be interpreted as a fixed ranking of every person's worth. Its meaning depends on the situation and the
relationships between those present.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Төрге шығыңыз — please take the place of honour.
     ●​   Төрге шығару — to invite someone to the place of honour.
     ●​   Төрлетіңіз — please come in and take the honoured seat.
     ●​   Төрде отыру — to sit in the place of honour.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Place of honour: The most accurate translation in cultural explanations.
     ●​   Honoured seat: Natural when referring to a particular seat.
     ●​   Head of the room: Sometimes useful spatially, but it does not necessarily communicate the cultural significance.
     ●​   Front of the house: Potentially misleading because tör is traditionally opposite the entrance, not necessarily at the
          front.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Tör is the traditionally honoured area of a Kazakh home or yurt, usually located opposite the entrance. During a visit, a host
may invite a respected guest or elder to sit there as a sign of hospitality and recognition. The phrase төрге шығыңыз is
therefore more than a direction to sit in a particular place: it communicates that the guest is being welcomed and honoured. The
position also illustrates how the arrangement of domestic space can express social relationships. In English, “place of honour”
is generally more informative than a literal translation such as “upper part of the room.” The practice should be explained as a
customary convention, not as an identical seating rule in every household.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   “Linguocultural Characteristics of Guest Hosting Traditions of Kazakh and Turkish People.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General context of hospitality and traditional guest-reception practices. Direct page-level evidence for the
          precise location and customary use of төр has not yet been established.
     ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialist ethnographic source describing the interior arrangement of the yurt
          and the social meaning of төр is required.

heading: QAMSHY

category.title: Material Culture and Traditional Lifestyle
category.description: Objects, spaces and art forms in traditional cultural life.

short: Qamshy refers to a traditional whip, commonly made with a handle and a braided leather lash.

sections.Identification:
●​   Kazakh: Қамшы
     ●​   Latin transliteration: Qamshy
     ●​   Pronunciation (IPA): /qɑmˈʃɯ/ (approximate)
     ●​   Word class: Noun
     ●​   Related forms: Қамшыгер (qamshyger, a person skilled in the use of a whip); қамшы өру (qamshy ör u, to braid a
          whip); қамшы сабы (qamshy saby, whip handle); қамшы салу (qamshy salu, to strike or use a whip, depending on
          context).
sections.Linguistic meaning:
Qamshy refers to a traditional whip, commonly made with a handle and a braided leather lash. It was used in horse riding and
livestock-related activities. Its construction, materials, and decorative features could vary.
sections.Cultural context:
The qamshy was a practical object associated with horsemanship and pastoral life. It could be used to guide or urge a horse
and was also made as a crafted object with decorative elements. In some historical and social contexts, it could carry symbolic
meanings connected with authority, status, or customary interaction. These symbolic interpretations should be supported by
specific historical evidence rather than assumed for every whip or every occasion.
sections.Social function:
The qamshy served practical purposes in riding and livestock management. It could also appear in customary settings and
social interactions, where its presence or use might communicate a particular intention. The meaning of such gestures
depended on the context and should not be generalised into one universal code.
sections.Cultural values:
Possible associations include horsemanship, practical skill, craftsmanship, mobility, and traditional pastoral life. In certain
contexts, it may also be associated with authority or social symbolism. However, it should not be presented as exclusively
ceremonial: its everyday practical function was significant.
sections.Practical application:
●​   Қамшы ұстау — to hold a whip.
     ●​   Қамшы өру — to braid a whip.
     ●​   Қамшымен ат айдау — to guide or urge a horse with a whip.
     ●​   Қамшыгер — a person skilled in using a whip.
     ●​   Қамшы салу — to strike or use a whip; the exact meaning depends on context.
sections.Translation analysis:
●​   Whip: The direct and most common English equivalent.
     ●​   Riding whip: More precise when describing its use in horsemanship.
     ●​   Braided leather whip: Useful when explaining its traditional construction.
     ●​   Ceremonial whip: Appropriate only when a particular object or use is demonstrably ceremonial.
     ●​   Symbol of authority: An interpretive description, not a direct translation.
sections.Cultural transfer:
Qamshy is a traditional whip associated with horse riding and pastoral life. It was generally made with a handle and a braided
leather lash, although its materials and design could vary. Its practical function was to help guide or urge a horse. Some
examples were also carefully decorated, demonstrating leatherworking and craft skills. In particular historical or customary
settings, the qamshy could carry meanings beyond its practical use, but these meanings should be explained through evidence
about the specific practice. It would be misleading to describe every qamshy as a ceremonial object or a universal symbol of
authority. For international readers, the most useful approach is to introduce it first as a riding whip and then explain its
additional cultural associations where documented.
sections.Evidence:
●​   Zhetpysbaev, S. K. (2023). “Traditions and Customs of the Kazakh People: Place and Role in the Modernization of
          Society.” Research PDF
     ●​   Supports: General context of traditional Kazakh lifestyle and material culture. It is not sufficient to verify the technical
          construction or all historical symbolic uses of the qamshy.
 ●​   Verification status: Preliminary draft. A specialist ethnographic or material-culture source on the qamshy, its
     construction, practical use, and documented symbolic functions is required.
